title: LIVE SURFACE CURRENTS
source_name: NOAA/NOS Great Lakes Operational Forecast System (GLOFS: LSOFS/LMHOFS/LEOFS/LOOFS) surface-current nowcast + NOAA/GLERL experimental GLCFS-FVCOM Huron-Erie Corridor & lower St. Marys River nowcast fill
variable: u_eastward / v_northward surface-layer velocity components (filed m/s, direction of water motion TOWARD); speed = sqrt(U^2+V^2), displayed in cm/s; direction arrows follow the filed (U,V) movement vector with no reversal
coverage: Five Great Lakes + Mackinac Straits + upper St. Marys River (operational GLOFS) + St. Clair River / Lake St. Clair / Detroit River (experimental HEC FVCOM) + lower St. Marys River (experimental Michigan-Huron FVCOM). Documented gaps: St. Marys rapids/locks reach, Niagara Falls/gorge reach, other minor canals.
arrows: Arrows show the toward-motion vector of the filed (U,V) components (CF eastward/northward sea-water velocity: no FROM/TOWARD reversal). White shaft with dark outline, uniform length; speed lives in the color gradient only.
what: How fast the surface water is moving right now (color = speed) and which way it is flowing (arrows). Covers all five Great Lakes plus the connecting rivers and channels where NOAA models provide current vectors.
why_extreme: Open-lake drift (a few cm/s, blue) owns most of the color resolution; river/channel jets to 100+ cm/s compress into red/dark-purple.
